# docs: add ownership guidance to house rules and the PR procedure

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to the parent issue or its siblings.

## What

Write down where each kind of code belongs, so contributors and agents put new code in the right
place without having to ask.

## Why

The upcoming restructuring moves code between owners. Unless the rules explain the reasoning,
later changes will drift back to the old layout.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, GitHub, files, containers, terminal, logging), `app` (use cases) and `cli` (commands).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

This issue implements one part of the design in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. That file is
in the repository; read the sections named below. Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow
the spec and say so in the PR.

## Don't undo these

- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image. The one exception:
  `jig init` saves a credential to `.jig/.env` (owner-only, git-ignored) after the operator agrees.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged unless this issue says otherwise.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.
- If you change where something lives, update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`
  and the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any guide that names a moved path. Describe current
  behavior in the present tense.

## Target

Spec sections: "Target responsibilities", "Error ownership and technical failure handling",
"House rules and review".

- `.claude/rules/callee-owns-its-rules.md`, `.claude/rules/errors-as-values.md`,
  `.claude/rules/parse-input-at-the-edge.md`: add short ownership guidance with concrete examples:
  - CLI does not receive a container or cradle; it calls an application operation and presents the result.
  - Configurable defaults (for example the step retry count) are not domain rules; domain consumes
    resolved `RunSettings`.
  - A capability failure (storage, Git, sandbox) belongs with its port contract, not in domain just
    because several modules return it.
  - Composition only wires: it chooses implementations and starts the executable, and makes no
    resume, retry, locking or publication decisions.
- `.claude/skills/commit-pr/SKILL.md` and `.github/pull_request_template.md`: a PR that changes
  ownership states the owner, why the concept belongs there, and whether it introduces a pattern
  agents should copy. Add this to the existing procedure; do not create a parallel guide.
- Also update `.agents/` copies of these rules or skills if they exist and are tracked.

This issue changes documentation only. Do not move code, and do not enforce ownership through
names (such as `DEFAULT_*`) or tests that check prose.

## Done when

- [ ] The rules above carry the four examples, each in the rule that owns it.
- [ ] The PR procedure and template ask for an ownership rationale.
- [ ] `npm run format:check` and `npm run lint` pass.


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/54

context.repoSummary: jig is a TypeScript CLI using Commander, Zod, Awilix and better-result. This slice changes only three existing house rules, the commit-pr skill and the PR template. docs/specs/application-boundaries.md describes target ownership, while docs/architecture.html documents the current implementation; do not implement the broader restructuring. Current rules contain examples needing reconciliation: callee-owns-its-rules.md references app/container.ts and cradle access; parse-input-at-the-edge.md shows an application operation receiving AwilixContainer; errors-as-values.md directs new failures into domain/errors.ts. Current CLI handlers actually receive containers, and domain/settings.ts holds retry defaults alongside RunSettings. Add CLI/application and composition-only-wiring guidance to callee ownership, config-owned defaults versus resolved domain settings to edge parsing, and port-owned storage/Git/sandbox failures to error guidance. Preserve Result/panic semantics and distinguish genuine domain safety rules from configurable defaults. The existing commit-pr procedure requires filling every PR-template section; extend it and the template to request the owner, ownership rationale and whether a reusable agent pattern is introduced. No tracked .agents copies exist. Do not move code, add scanners or prose tests, or change runtime behavior. Required implementation checks are npm run format:check (Prettier) and npm run lint (ESLint).

plan.summary: Update the three existing house rules, commit-pr procedure, and PR template with concise ownership guidance and concrete examples. This is documentation-only work; runtime behavior and source locations remain unchanged.
plan.approach: Use the spec’s Target responsibilities, Error ownership and technical failure handling, and House rules and review sections as authority. In callee ownership, explain that CLI receives application operations rather than containers or cradles, and composition selects implementations and starts the executable without deciding resume, retry, locking, or publication policy. Replace contradictory examples that encourage cradle access. In edge parsing, distinguish config-owned schemas and configurable defaults, such as step retry counts, from genuine domain safety rules; domain consumes resolved RunSettings. Replace the AwilixContainer application-operation example while preserving parse-once guidance. In error guidance, replace the blanket instruction to add failures to domain/errors.ts with ownership by meaning: business failures in domain, portable storage/Git/sandbox failures with their port contracts, and raw exception translation in adapters. Preserve Result/panic semantics and narrow failure contracts. Extend the existing PR procedure and template’s How guidance to require the owner, why the concept belongs there, and whether it introduces a reusable pattern agents should copy. Explicitly reconcile current-versus-target mismatches during design: CLI currently receives containers, app/container.ts mixes wiring and lifecycle policy, domain/settings.ts holds retry defaults, and domain/errors.ts centralizes technical failures. The spec also selects a dedicated composition owner whereas current guidance names app/container.ts and AGENTS.md restricts Awilix to app; describe the target responsibility without claiming relocation has occurred or deciding the deferred construction mechanism. No tracked .agents copies exist. Keep current architecture maps unchanged because this slice moves no code. Review the documentation for consistency, then run npm run format:check and npm run lint; add no source scanners, naming enforcement, or prose tests.
affectedAreas: .claude/rules/callee-owns-its-rules.md — CLI/application boundary and composition-only wiring guidance and examples
.claude/rules/parse-input-at-the-edge.md — config-owned defaults, resolved RunSettings, and container-free application example
.claude/rules/errors-as-values.md — capability failure ownership while preserving Result/panic behavior
.claude/skills/commit-pr/SKILL.md — ownership rationale requirement in the existing PR procedure
.github/pull_request_template.md — owner, rationale, and reusable agent-pattern prompts
